discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, including giant TMR in MgO-barrier junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

motivation: In 1995 Moodera and Miyazaki independently showed large, reproducible tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/insulator/ferromagnet junctions. Spin-dependent tunnelling thereby became a practical physical effect rather than a low-temperature curiosity. Parkin then demonstrated giant TMR through crystalline MgO barriers (2004), where coherent tunnelling via symmetry-filtered Bloch states yields magnetoresistance of hundreds of percent. Magnetic tunnel junctions are the basis of every modern hard-disk read head and of MRAM. STT-MRAM is now embedded in commercial foundry processes. Having worked on the first commercial MRAM, I can attest that this physics reached large-scale manufacturing. The same junctions made spin-torque oscillators, spintronic sensors and neuromorphic spintronic elements possible. The discovery pairs new quantum-transport physics with lasting impact on information technology, following naturally from the 2007 Prize for giant magnetoresistance.
